scope: 584 nonempty battle-effect overlay containers from PAL disc group 0x11; movie buffers excluded.
working_estimate: Approximately 15 MiB of stored EE instructions, including repeated code across overlay containers. Heuristic estimate, not an exact linked .text size.
method: Decode both packed formats using the game decoder algorithms.
Seed control flow from the seven main callback vectors, plausible additional callback pointers in the first 0x100 bytes, and stack prologues followed by a saved return address.
Follow direct calls and branches with MIPS delay slots; stop at returns, unresolved indirect jumps, invalid/implausible encodings and long zero padding.

Where the header resource pointer is valid, restrict analysis to the prefix preceding embedded resource data; otherwise use full payload. No discovered direct targets crossed a valid resource boundary.
Count the union of detected instruction addresses once per container.
Partition detected instructions at inferred entry candidates, hash each resulting raw-byte piece and sum distinct hashes as an exact-byte repetition metric.
limitations: Not a full disassembly or certified function inventory. Inferred entry candidates are not a reliable function count.
1171 unresolved indirect-jump sites can hide switch cases or additional code.
The 16.7 MiB occupied-address span includes holes and possibly embedded data, and is not an exact code-size upper bound.
The 6.6 MiB exact-byte metric is not a semantic unique-code count: relocated copies may differ, and inferred routine boundaries can split functions. It cannot directly measure decompilation workload.
Container sizes include textures, animation and other data and must not be treated as executable-code sizes.
